newsitem.title: HONG KONG: U.S. grants 10-year visas to post-97 HK residents.
newsitem.headline: U.S. grants 10-year visas to post-97 HK residents.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it would grant 10-year multiple-entry visas to holders of new Hong Kong passports after China takes the territory back from Britain in July.

U.S. Consul-General Richard Boucher, announcing the move at a news conference, said holders of Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (SAR) passports would get the same visa treatment now enjoyed by holders of Hong Kong British passports.

The decision was a milestone in the international recognition of SAR passports and removed a question mark hanging over Hong Kong as China prepares to resume sovereignty at midnight on June 30, ending 156 years of British colonial rule.
Winning easy visa access to major Western countries is viewed as a barometer of confidence in the territory's future stability. Hong Kong has a population of 6.4 million people.
"We intend to issue maximum validity visas for the United States for the people with the new Hong Kong Special Administrative Region passport," Boucher said.
This privilege is currently enjoyed by holders of British National Overseas (BNOC) passports with ease, while holders of Hong Kong travel documents face tough screening when they apply for visas.
